Two preview-template fixes in /opt/nxeon-staging (staging).

TEMPLATE 1 — Domains (`components/marketing/domainstemplate/*`, `/preview/domains`): the hero domain-search motion graphic currently loops a canned demo. Change it to: **play the auto-demo ONCE, then hand control to the user** — the search bar becomes a real, interactive domain checker they can type into and check availability. Wire it to the real availability check if one exists (grep for a domain-availability server action / API — e.g. `lib/actions-domain*`, `app/api/domains/*`, or the existing `DomainChecker` showcase component's data source); if no live check is reachable from a preview, do a realistic deterministic client-side availability read (clearly the same UX). After the one-time demo animation finishes, the field must be focusable/typeable and return a result per query.

TEMPLATE 2 — Location (`components/marketing/locationtemplate/*`, `/preview/location`): replace the SVG-mockup country markers with **real HD country flag images**. Source flags from flagcdn (HD PNGs: `https://flagcdn.com/w1280/<iso2>.png`, e.g. sg, id, my, ph, th, hk, au, jp) via `curl` into `public/flags/<iso2>.png`, and render those. Keep the animated latency map/bars; just swap the flag visuals to real HD flags. Make it generic so other location pages (other cities/countries) can reference `/flags/<iso2>.png`.

SHARED (apply to BOTH): Replace any plain star/StarRow with EXISTING `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx`. Replace emoji glyphs with `components/marketing/icons.tsx`. Proper metadata + JSON-LD. Do NOT edit `app/globals.css` (CSS Modules/inline; reuse `pv-*`). Own-template files only + your own `public/flags/` assets. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Do NOT run `npm run build`/dev server. Report changes + flags downloaded.

**`components/marketing/domainstemplate/DomainsLanding.tsx`** — reworked the hero `DomainSearchPanel`:

When it returns usable data (logged-in / registrar configured) it renders real results. When it isn't reachable from a preview (401 for a logged-out visitor, `configured:false`, rate-limited, or network error) it falls back to a **deterministic client-side read** (`buildDeterministic`, reusing the existing hash-based `avail()` + `POPULAR_TLDS` prices) — same UX, always returns a result per query, including handling a fully-typed `name.tld`.
